scope: Offline protocol review only. This file does not execute target operations. Root agent owns execution and user authorization.
purpose: First validate a brief A7 CPU0 halt/resume through generic MEM-AP, with no framebuffer change, instruction injection, CPU register reads/writes, cache maintenance, peripheral clock/reset change, or Flash/RAM write.

observed.OSLSR_decode: OSLM split bits3,0 = 0b10 (OS Lock implemented, no OSSRR); OSLK bit1 =1 (locked)

AUTHSTATUS_decode.limitation: Authentication inputs permit invasive debug in both security states. This is not proof that a particular system-bus write bypasses Software/OS Lock.

observed.DSCR_decode: HALTED0, RESTARTED1, HDBGen0, ITRen0, ExtDCCmode0, sticky exceptions0; bit24 is UNKNOWN while running and must not be used as a pre-halt gate
observed.PRSR_decode: PU1, SPD1, R0, SR1, HALTED0, OSLK1, DLK0; SPD/SR can be historical and their read-clear side effects are suppressed while Software Lock is set
observed.LSR_decode: Software Lock implemented bit0=1 and set bit1=1; nTT bit2=0
observed.CMU_decode: Both implemented DBGEN/SPIDEN/NIDEN/SPNIDEN signal fields are set. Do not modify this register for the halt/resume test.

sequence.operation: Use the existing generic mem_ap target. Read fresh ECR/LSR/OSLSR/AUTH/DSCR/PRSR and record original lock states.
sequence.gates: CPU was running, AUTH low8=ff, ECR bit0=0, PRSR.PU=1/R=0/DLK=0, DSCR.ITRen=0, sticky exceptions=0. For this simplest test require DSCR writable controls mask0x0030fc00=0. Do not gate on running InstrCompl bit24.

sequence.operation: Set lar_write_possible flag before issuing DBGLAR=c5acce55. Read DBGLSR and require SLI1/SLK0 (low3=1 for this view).
sequence.failure: If unchanged locked or read/write fails, do not continue to OS unlock or HRQ. Cleanup can attempt DBGLAR=0 to re-establish original Software Lock, and must verify if readable.

sequence.operation: After confirmed Software unlock, read PRSR once to record/ack historical SPD/SR, then immediately read it again to establish a live baseline.
sequence.gates: Second read requires PU1,R0,DLK0,SPD0,SR0; then arm reset/power-loss tracking. The first post-unlock read's historical bits must not be interpreted as test-induced reset. Neither CPU was halted nor HRQ issued yet.

sequence.operation: Set oslar_write_possible flag before issuing DBGOSLAR=0. Read OSLSR and PRSR, require OSLK0 in both. Check reset/power tracker and AUTH still enabled.
sequence.failure: Never advance if OS unlock failed. Restore OS Lock first while Software Lock remains clear, then Software Lock. If CPU unexpectedly halted after unlock, treat it as a possible debug-state transition and use the guarded resume cleanup, not an unconditional relock.

sequence.operation: Read fresh DSCR/PRSR. If still running with the gated controls, set hrq_write_possible before issuing DBGDRCR=1. Poll DSCR.HALTED until 1 using a bounded deadline; interleave PRSR reads for live reset/power status.
sequence.note: No HDBGen write is needed for this Halt request. Official Arm CSAT A7 example halts using DRCR.HRQ before its optional HDBGen configuration.
sequence.timeout: A zero write to DRCR is not a cancellation. HRQ is held until Debug state entry. If the request times out, do not report successful rollback merely because the CPU currently reads running.

sequence.operation: When halted, read DSCR/PRSR again. Require DSCR.HALTED1 and PRSR.HALTED1, InstrCompl bit24=1, ITRen0, stable power/reset tracker. Record the halt time and DSCR method-of-entry bits5:2.
sequence.expected_MOE: 0 for HRQ; another method indicates a concurrent debug event and must be reported
sequence.hold: For this first control test, issue resume immediately after status capture. No intentional hold/sleep or screen writes. Timers/watchdogs/DMA and MCU execution are not halted by CPU0 halt.

sequence.operation: Set rrq_write_possible before issuing DBGDRCR=6 (RRQ bit1 plus CSE bit2), with bit4 Cancel Bus Requests always 0. Poll until DSCR.HALTED0 and RESTARTED1; verify PRSR.HALTED0 and no reset/power-loss latch.
sequence.resume_gate: Only when the CPU is actually halted, InstrCompl1 and ITRen0. Record sticky-exception bits before CSE. No ITR/DTR access or PC/CPSR restoration is needed because no instruction/register transfer was performed.

sequence.operation: Once running is verified, restore original OS Lock first: DBGOSLAR=c5acce55, verify OSLSR.OSLK1. Then restore original Software Lock: DBGLAR=0, verify DBGLSR.SLK1.
sequence.note: Lock registers are write-only; restore their Boolean lock state, not an imagined saved register value.

sequence.operation: Read DSCR/PRSR once after relock to verify running and record final observation; compare only meaningful writable control bits, not full DSCR status against the pre-halt word.
sequence.success: A7 confirmed halted then resumed, both original locks restored, no test-interval reset/power loss, no injected instructions or core registers changed.

catch_cleanup_rules: Maintain possible-write flags before issuing each mutation, including lock changes and HRQ/RRQ, because a failing AP transfer can have committed the target write.

Use one PRSR-read helper for every read after the live baseline is armed. Latch PU0, R1, SR1, SPD1 or DLK1; repeated reads can clear sticky bits and must not erase the software latch. Initial historic SPD/SR are recorded separately.
When cleanup begins, get fresh power/reset, lock, and DSCR state. Do not blindly replay old DSCR or CPU register data. No CPU register snapshot or restoration is part of this protocol.
If our temporary unlock may have led to a halt, and a fresh consistent status proves powered/stable halted, ITRen0 and InstrCompl1, send DRCR6 once and verify running before restoring either lock.
If already running and HRQ was never possibly issued, restore OS Lock then Software Lock and verify; this is a complete lock-only rollback.

If HRQ may have been issued but halt was never observed, a running read alone does not prove there is no pending request. A bounded continued observation may catch a late halt and perform the guarded resume. If it remains uncertain, mark incomplete recovery; do not invent a DRCR cancellation or use reset/clock/power controls as silent cleanup.

Do not relock OS/Software debug access while a halted core still needs a restart through that same system view. If resume cannot be confirmed, preserve diagnostic access and report the unresolved halted state instead of claiming restoration.

If reset/power loss occurred, do not treat the old execution state as valid or attempt PC/core-register restoration. Record the event and actual latest state. Recovery beyond the guarded debug resume is root/user owned.
If lock restoration fails, keep the precise current lock state in the result. A successful CPU resume does not by itself mean the entire temporary debug configuration was restored.
important_scope_limits: Only the identified CPU debug component at0x58050000 is controlled. This does not pause all cores, MCU, DMA, LCDC scanout, or the whole DSP power domain.

Pure halt/resume preserves the current architectural execution point without injected instructions, but changes elapsed time and debug status. It is not a rollback of peripheral timers, interrupts, DMA traffic, exclusive-monitor behavior, or firmware timeouts.

The public ROM table at0x58040000 has a first entry0x00020003 pointing at0x58060000. This does not invalidate the directly verified Cortex-A7 IDs at0x58050000, but the incomplete ROM capture does not establish cluster/core count.
